commits.edited_message:
color-conversion: guard chroma bit depth in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa

Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa reads the Cb/Cr planes through a uint16_t* using
a sample width taken from the Y channel, but never checked the chroma bit
depth. convert_colorspace() already rejects YCbCr images whose chroma
planes are shallower than the luma plane (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), so this
is defense in depth: refuse a chroma plane deeper than the luma plane,
which the luma-derived read would silently truncate, so this operator
stays self-contained should a future direct caller or pipeline change
bypass the central guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let color-conversion operators declare the sample width they read

The operators picked uint8_t or uint16_t samples from an 8-bit SDR/HDR split
(bits_per_pixel > 8 meant "two bytes per sample"). That dates from when 16 bits
was the maximum and is wrong for the 32-, 64- and 128-bit components that
'unci' can carry: HeifPixelImage stores those with 4, 8 or 16 bytes per sample.
Nothing wider than 16 bits could reach an operator, because each of them
guarded against it separately through has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and
convert_colorspace() has a backstop, but the sample type never followed the
allocation, so those guards were load-bearing.

Make the sample width explicit instead. bytes_per_sample_for_bit_depth() in
pixelimage.h is now the single mapping from bit depth to storage width, used
by plane allocation and by the operators, so the two cannot drift. ColorState
gained get_bytes_per_sample(), get_max_bytes_per_sample(),
color_channels_have_bytes_per_sample() and all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(),
and each operator declares in state_after_conversion() which sample width it
can read (sizeof(Pixel) for the templated ones; the fixed-width ones bound the
width they read). Strides are
divided by the sample width instead of by a conditional 2, alpha rows are
copied with their own width, and the operators that switch on the width at
runtime refuse anything else. has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and the
all_channels_sdr()/all_channels_hdr() helpers have no callers left and are
removed; the check added for GHSA-r7gr-2xm2-23wf in Op_flatten_alpha_plane
becomes all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(sizeof(Pixel)).

The 16-bit backstop and the YCbCr luma/chroma check in convert_colorspace()
now also run when no pipeline could be built, so callers keep getting the
specific error instead of the generic "unsupported color conversion".

A new test builds 32-, 64- and 128-bit YCbCr, RGB and monochrome states and
checks that the operators decline them and that no pipeline is constructible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Declare the shared colour depth in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every plane
on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already did for
RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8 converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards already
returned InternalError for mixed depths), and Op_YCbCr420_to_RGB24 and
Op_YCbCr420_to_RGB32 test the uniform colour depth instead of the luma depth
alone. Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa keeps its luma test: its inline guard already
pins the chroma bit depths against the luma depth.
With every YCbCr operator declaring the constraint, the entry check is
removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target (no operator can widen the 8-bit chroma planes),
now with the generic Unsupported_color_conversion subcode, and adds the two
8-bit routes that succeed: interleaved RGB, and the native layout with
convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose samples are checked exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa reads the Cb/Cr planes through a uint16_t* whose sample width is derived from the luma bit depth, so converting a YCbCr 4:2:0 image with 16-bit luma but 8-bit chroma (a layout 'unci' files may declare per component) over-reads each 1-byte/sample chroma plane by two bytes per sample (ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace). The original batch blocks that route with three independent layers, each introduced by one of the edited commits, and all three must be relaxed for the bug to be reachable: (1) commit 7749246's runtime guard in convert_colorspace() is narrowed from 'chroma depth != luma depth' to 'chroma depth > luma depth', so a shallower chroma plane is let through -- benign when written, because the central convert_colorspace() entry check then still rejected every luma/chroma mismatch, so the guard's direction was unobservable; (2) commit e439543's plan-time declaration 'all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(2)' is weakened to a maximum-width check (get_max_bytes_per_sample() > 2), which a 16/8/8 image passes -- benign in its own commit because the uniform-depth plan test added later still declines such images, and plausible because the inline guard was believed to pin the chroma depths; (3) commit 68daf78's uniform-depth plan test (get_uniform_color_bits_per_pixel() <= 8) is kept as the luma-only test (bits_per_pixel_Y <= 8) for this one operator, so the planner now offers the operator for 16-bit luma regardless of the chroma depth -- benign in its own commit because both the width declaration and the runtime guard still rejected the mismatch. Consequently a correct fix must restore the cross-layer invariant in more than one place: reverting any one commit's edit leaves at least one of the other two layers intact and the conversion is still refused cleanly (verified by building all three single-edit and all three pair-edit trees: the probe is refused with heif_suberror_Unsupported_color_conversion on every one of them). Only the composition of all three edited commits lets the 16/8/8 image reach the uint16_t chroma read.
